title: H-Index
summary: Given an array of integers representing the number of citations for each of a researcher's papers, determine the h-index, which is the maximum number of papers that have at least as many citations as their rank.
statement: Given an array of integers representing the number of citations for each of a researcher's papers, determine the h-index, which is the maximum number of papers that have at least as many citations as their rank.
constraints: Return the largest h for which at least h papers each have at least h citations. Papers beyond those h may have any citation count.
hints: Citation values above the paper count are equivalent for h-index purposes.
Bucket each citation at min(citation,n), then scan candidate h values downward.
Accumulate the number of papers in buckets h through n; the first h with accumulated papers≥h is maximal.
This avoids sorting and handles one enormous citation count without mistaking it for many papers.
editorial: An h-index cannot exceed the number of papers, so every larger citation count can share one final bucket. Scanning buckets from n downward maintains exactly how many papers have at least the current candidate. The first feasible candidate is the maximum. The independent oracle directly tries every h and recounts qualifying papers.

tests.explanation: Three papers have at least 3 citations, while fewer than four papers have at least 4, so h=3.
Only one paper has at least two citations, but all three conditions for h=1 are met, so h=1.
